# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a male parent who supplies the seed of the child's conception. The KJV text says the child's conception was *of the Holy Ghost*, within a virgin, with no man involved. Joseph was husband, legal father and guardian, but not begetter.

## 1. The text states the mode of conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together," is the verb for the couple's union. The text places the conception before that union. *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 + G4151 + G40), "out of the Holy Ghost," gives the source of the pregnancy with the preposition *ek*, "out of," marking origin.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *to gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "that which is begotten or conceived," is the same root used for the human "begats" of Matthew 1. Here the begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost, not to a man.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before any union with Joseph. Matthew 1:20, through *gennaō* with *ek*, assigns the origin of the conceived child to the Holy Ghost. So no human male is the origin of the child, which excludes a biological human father. This rests on two [L1] verses and two [L2] grounds.

## 2. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual knowledge. *anēr* (G435) is "a man," a male. Mary is betrothed, so the question concerns the manner of conception, not the future.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow," and *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon," describe divine action. *dio kai* (G1352), "therefore also," makes the divine action the stated reason for the title.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Mary is called a virgin before the angel speaks.

**[L4]** The angel answers "how" with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not with a man. Luke 1:27 says she was a virgin and Luke 1:34 says she knew no man. Together these show the angel's answer replaces human paternity. A biological father would not need "therefore" to ground the title.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link in Matthew 1 uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a male subject. At the last link the verb becomes passive, *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *ex hēs* (G1537), "out of whom," is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," not begetter.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L4]** The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph, and the birth is "of whom," feminine, namely Mary. Matthew 1:25 repeats the verb *ginōskō*, "know," for Joseph and Mary, and says he did not know her until the child was born. The verse and the Greek grammar together show Joseph's role changes from begetter to husband.

## 4. Joseph's reaction and the "as was supposed"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L4]** Joseph knew he had not fathered the child, and resolved to put Mary away until the angel spoke. This is Joseph's own judgment on the facts, and it is corrected only by the angel, who says the child is "of the Holy Ghost," not by any claim that Joseph was the father.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "was reckoned, was supposed by custom," marks the common opinion as an opinion, not as the truth.

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd's claim, matching Luke 3:23's "as was supposed." Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary speaks of Joseph as "thy father" by household usage, and the child answers with "my Father's business."

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels "son of Joseph" a supposition. The later passages show the same pattern: the crowd's talk and the household's talk use "father" of Joseph, but the child himself names another Father in Luke 2:49. The title is legal and customary, not a claim of begetting.

## 5. The prophecy and Paul's wording

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** *ʿalmāh* (H5959), "a young woman of marriageable age, unmarried," is rendered in Matthew 1:23 with *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Matthew 1:22 introduces it: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled."

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096 + G1537 + G1135), "become out of a woman," names only the mother as the human source. Compare Hebrews 10:5 [L3]: "a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L4]** Isaiah 7:14 requires a virgin conceiving, which Matthew 1:22-23 says was fulfilled. Galatians 4:4 names only a woman as the human origin of the son sent. Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23 and Galatians 4:4 together exclude a male human parent in the fulfilment.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The conception is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost" before Mary and Joseph "came together": Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:20 [L1], with *sunerchomai* (come together) and *gennaō* (begotten) with *ek* (out of) [L2].
2. Mary was a virgin who "know[s] not a man," and the angel answers with the Holy Ghost, not a man: Luke 1:34-35 [L1], with *ginōskō* (know) and *episkiazō* (overshadow) [L2], and Luke 1:27 [L3].
3. Matthew's genealogy ends with Joseph as *anēr* (husband), not begetter, and the birth is *ex hēs* (out of whom, feminine): Matthew 1:16 [L1], with *egennēsen*/*egennēthē* (begat/was born) [L2], and Matthew 1:25 [L3].
4. "Son of Joseph" is a supposition and a legal or household title: Luke 3:23 [L1], with *nomizō* (suppose) [L2], and Luke 2:48-49 and John 6:42 [L3].
5. Isaiah 7:14 and Galatians 4:4 require a virgin conception and name only a woman as the human source: Isaiah 7:14 [L1], with *ʿalmāh* (virgin, young woman) and *ek gynaikos* (out of a woman) [L2], and Matthew 1:23 [L3].
6. Therefore Christ had no biological human father: his conception was of the Holy Ghost in a virgin, and Joseph was husband and legal father only (Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 [L1]; *gennaō*, *ek* [L2]; Matthew 1:16, Galatians 4:4 [L3]).

# Challenge: the seed of David came out of a man's loins, and the man the text names is Joseph

The defender's chain stands on two readings. First, that "of the Holy Ghost" names the begetter of the flesh. Second, that the timing rows remove the husband. Neither reading fits the rows that state where the promised seed comes from, or by whose house its pedigree is counted. I press each link by its D-number, then set out my own chain.

---

## PRESS ON D1: "of the Holy Ghost" and "before they came together"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

**[L2]** The defender says *gennaō* (G1080, "beget") with *ek* (G1537, "out of") attributes the begetting to the Holy Ghost. The same verb with the same preposition is said of believers:

**[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]"

**[L3]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L2]** Romans 1:3 states fleshly origin differently: *ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka*, "of the seed (*sperma*, G4690) of David according to the flesh (*sarx*, G4561)." Matthew 1:20 carries *ek* with the Spirit and has no *kata sarka*.

**[L4]** The pattern is set by two kinds of evidence:
- the [L3] rows show *gennaō* + *ek* + God naming covenant origin in believers who have fleshly fathers;
- the [L2] contrast shows *kata sarka* is the marker the text adds when it means flesh.

So "of the Holy Ghost" is the covenant origin of the child. The same row names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." The verse is held whole, and the father of the house stands inside it.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Matthew sets what "came together" means by what follows. Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." The law names the same step: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" (Deuteronomy 20:7).

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18's *synelthein* (G4905, "come together") dates the *finding*: it came before the taking of Matthew 1:24. This is footed on Matthew 1:18 [L1], Matthew 1:24 [L3] and Deuteronomy 20:7 [L3]. The defender's D1 moves the conception outside the espousal. The rows date only the finding.

---

## PRESS ON D2: Luke 1:34-35

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *andra ou ginōskō*: *ginōskō* (G1097) is present active indicative. It states her condition at the moment the angel spoke.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** The two verbs of Luke 1:35 have their own uses elsewhere:
- *eperchomai* (G1904, "come upon") is said of the apostles. Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me … [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]."
- *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow") is the transfiguration cloud: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them" (Luke 9:34). It is also Peter's shadow: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them" (Acts 5:15).

These rows read as power and presence.

**[L3]** The "therefore" points back to the title already given. The dio kai ('therefore') in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and "the throne of his father David" come before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.

**[L3]** The title stands beside a fleshly father in one verse. 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."

**[L4]** Footed on Luke 1:32-35 [L1], *dio kai*, *eperchomai* and *episkiazō* [L2], and 1 Chronicles 28:6 [L3]: the "therefore" grounds a covenant title. Solomon bore that title with David as his begetter. The defender's sentence "A biological father would not need 'therefore' to ground the title" is answered by 1 Chronicles 28:6, which gives "thy son" and "my son" in one breath.

---

## PRESS ON D3: Matthew 1:16 and its feminine "of whom"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L3]** Matthew uses the same construction, *ek* + feminine, for mothers whose husbands are named as begetters in the same line:
- Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;"
- Matthew 1:5: "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;"

**[L2]** *ek tēs Thamar*, *ek tēs Rhachab*, *ek tēs Rhouth* are *ek* (G1537) with a feminine object. This is the same form as *ex hēs* at 1:16, and in each case it stands beside a male begetter.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." *heōs hou* (G2193, "till") bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.

**[L4]** Footed on Matthew 1:3, 5 [L3] and *ek tēs* [L2]: Matthew's feminine *ek* names the mother and leaves the man beside her. Matthew 1:16 does not narrate the begetting. Its passive *egennēthē* fits the man named in the same verse as "Joseph the husband of Mary." That fits my link.

---

## PRESS ON D4: Joseph's intent and "as was supposed"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L2]** *dikaios ōn … eboulēthē lathra apolysai autēn*, "being just … was minded to put her away privily." Matthew gives an intent (*boulomai*, G1014) and two grounds. The verse contains no verb of knowing. The defender's "Joseph knew he had not fathered the child" adds a knowledge-verb the row does not carry.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli,"

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*, "to do by law (usage), be wont") appears in the same form at Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." That use reports a custom and makes no judgment of falsehood.

**[L3]** Mary speaks to the child in her own voice: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48). The narrator says the same: "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41). Luke 2:49, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?", names the covenant Father of 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." The covenant Father stands beside the fleshly father, as it does at 1 Chronicles 28:6.

**[L4]** Footed on Luke 3:23 [L1], *nomizō* at Acts 16:13 [L2], and Luke 2:33, 41, 48 [L3]: Luke's reckoning by custom stands with Mary's own "thy father." Luke 2:49 adds the covenant Father, as 2 Samuel 7:14 does for David's son.

---

## PRESS ON D5: Isaiah 7:14 and Galatians 4:4

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"

**[L2]** The Hebrew word is *ha-ʿalmāh* (H5959). The same word is rendered "the maid" at Exodus 2:8 ("And the maid went and called the child's mother") and "a maid" at Proverbs 30:19 ("the way of a man with a maid"). The word that the text itself pairs with being untouched is *bethulah* (H1330). Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The defender's chain glosses *ʿalmāh* as "(virgin, young woman)"; the Hebrew rows give "maid."

**[L3]** The sign is bounded in Isaiah's own day. Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings." Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son."

**[L4]** Matthew 1:22-23 stands as written. Its "a virgin shall be with child" (*parthenos*, G3933) covers the time Matthew 1:25 defines: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Footed on Matthew 1:23 [L1], *parthenos* with *heōs hou* [L2], and Matthew 1:25 [L3]: the fulfilment describes Mary during the pregnancy after the taking. It fits a named father.

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,"

**[L3]** "Born of a woman" is the mortality idiom:
- Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"
- Job 15:14: "[he which is] born of a woman, that he should be righteous?"

The same idiom is said of John (Matthew 11:11), whose father the angel addresses: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).

**[L4]** Footed on Galatians 4:4 [L1] and Job 14:1, 15:14 and Luke 1:13 [L3]: "made of a woman" marks mortality and subjection, "made under the law." It is said of men whose fathers are named.

---

## THE KEYSTONE D6 AGAINST THE SEED ROWS

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."

**[L2]** *zeraʿ* (H2233) means "seed, posterity." *mimmeʿeykha*, from *meʿeh* (H4578), means "out of thy bowels, inward parts."

**[L3]** The promise is repeated in bodily terms:
- Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The word is *osphys* (G3751, "loins, procreative power"). It is the word of Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."
- Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**[L3]** The law counts pedigree by the house of the fathers:
- Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls."
- Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- Ezra 2:61-62 shows the opposite case. Priests "called after their name" of a wife's house "sought their register … but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

**[L3]** The house of David rests on Joseph in these rows: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27, *ex oikou Dauid* following *Iōsēph*); "because he was of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). For Mary, the rows give a kinswoman: "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).

**[L4]** Footed on 2 Samuel 7:12 and Hebrews 7:14 [L1], *zeraʿ*, *osphys* and *sperma kata sarka* [L2], and Numbers 1:2, 18, Ezra 2:61-62 and Luke 2:4 [L3]: the promised seed comes "out of thy bowels" and "of the fruit of his loins." Its tribe is "evident" by the reckoning of the fathers' house. The house the rows give is Joseph's.

**Question to the defender:** According to Hebrews 7:14, how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given the law of Numbers 1:2 and 1:18, "by the house of their fathers"?

---

## MY DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's loins and bowels, according to the flesh.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30
- [L2] *zeraʿ* (seed), *meʿeh* (bowels), *osphys* (loins), *sperma kata sarka* (seed according to the flesh)
- [L3] Romans 1:3; Hebrews 7:10; Psalm 132:11

**C2. The pedigree is evident by the father's house, and the house of David in the rows is Joseph's.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14
- [L2] *oikos* (G3624, house) and *patria* (G3965, lineage) at Luke 2:4
- [L3] Numbers 1:2, 18; Ezra 2:61-62; Luke 1:27

**C3. The father is named in four voices.**
- [L1] Mary: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48). The town: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42). Philip: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45). The angel: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- [L3] Joseph names the child, the father's act: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21 [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]), done at 1:25. Compare "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called" (Luke 1:62).

**C4. "Of the Holy Ghost," "come upon" and "overshadow" are covenant origin, power and presence. "Son of God" is the covenant title.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20; Luke 1:32, 35
- [L2] *gennaō* + *ek*; *eperchomai*; *episkiazō*; *dio kai*
- [L3] 1 John 5:1; Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; 1 Chronicles 28:6

**C5. [L4] Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.** Footing:
- The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing. Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" [L1], with *yadaʿ* (H3045, "know") [L2].
- They were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24) [L3].
- The timing rows fit inside this chain. "Before they came together" dates the finding before the taking of Matthew 1:24. "I know not a man" is her present state when the angel spoke. "Knew her not till she had brought forth" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking.

**C6. Therefore Christ had a biological father, Joseph of the house of David.**
- [L1] Romans 1:3; Luke 2:48
- [L2] *sperma*, *osphys*
- [L3] Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:2

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

ASSUMES: *gennaō* + *ek* with the Spirit names the begetter of the flesh.

# Link round: the defender's answers

The challenger's list carries its verses under "ROWS GIVE", not under a "PRESSED WITH" label (ruling 392). I answer every one of them anyway, quoting each.

## LINK D1: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God" (1 John 5:1); "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3); "Joseph, thou son of David … Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** G1064 *gastēr*, "belly, womb," stands in the Greek of "with child." The conception is therefore a literal pregnancy in the womb. G4905 *synerchomai* is "come together … or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)." In Matthew 1:24 the "taking" is G3880 *paralambanō*, "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself." Matthew uses two different verbs. The challenger equates them without a row.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Joseph knew her not before the finding (1:18, before they came together). He knew her not after it (1:25). The challenger's own bounding of 1:25 to "the pregnancy after the taking" leaves the conception in the one gap where 1:18 says there was no coming together.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 (*synerchomai*, conjugal union, after the finding) and Matthew 1:25 (no knowing till the birth) together leave no union of Joseph and Mary before the birth. A conception "of the Holy Ghost" in that womb therefore has no human begetter beside it.
